This ruin used to be a major center of commerce because it had access to a major road and a huge waterway that fed out to the Great Black Sea. It boasted a fairly large population with lots of farmable land on either end. A sizable militia and a training ground. Now, it’s a ghost of what once was. It holds nothing but ruins and an old church. The church had been maintained as best as it could until a particularly intense attack. Now, the church has fallen.

### 		**Helmir**

Helmir was a place of learning. Many religious scholars had their homes there and taught there. Helmir is home to the Basilica of Light. This was an enormous church that held a great many services. It was also the seat of the Festival of Summer. A festival lasting two weeks where a great many citizens of Zweitenholm would visit and partake. It was said that a blessing during the Festival of Summer would grant the citizens happiness and health throughout the whole year. Even now, a group of Freemen attempt to hold Helmir against the encroaching tide of the Hollow Ones.

## 	**The Scarred Lands**

These lands once were filled with farmable land, homes and forests. In the last days of the battle to defend the wall, the defenders burned the land with regular fire and with magical flames. The landscape was left a battered, gray ruin with cracks down into the bowels of the earth everywhere. It often rains ash here and the voices of the many fallen can still be heard in the wind.

## 	**Beyond Nightsdeep**

Beyond is a whole world but it is unknown whether the Hollow Ones have consumed most of it or if this blight is contained in Jarn. What is known is that those who have attempted to leave the realm never return. Commonly, it is believed that beyond the realm the world is simply gone. A ruined husk not worthy of even exploring. Whether this is true or not is a true mystery.

### 		**Zvell, the frozen lands**

To the north are the frozen lands. An unforgivingly harsh place where the unwary traveller will simply freeze to death before even reaching a settlement. The Jotunnheimer tribe claim to originally come from these lands. It is known that there was a settlement called Niflheim. Nifleheim is supposed to be a marvelous city carved entirely from ice. In the morning, as the sun rose, the mist from the city was said to make it look like it was a dream.

### 		**The Norori Seas**

To the south west are the Norori seas. These unpredictable and tumultuous waters lead into the Ocean of Storms. Once, travel along the coast was the easiest way to get to points along the continent. Ships would come in and out constantly as trade was swift and prosperous. Now, the ships don’t come anymore and the floating Hollow Ones pull down anyone who dares to venture beyond the net. Still, the sea is an important waterway that connects Skaldfel, Darkholm and Dranet.

### 		**Brymja Sea**

The Brymja sea runs along the west of the peninsula. Its crystal clear waters aren’t quite as intense as the Norori sea but can be just as deadly. Within the net, the Brymja sea is mostly filled with fishermen as most of the big cities are closer to the Norori sea. Its waters are quite shallow all the way out to the net so fishermen either use special flatboats or simply stand in the shallower parts. Beyond the net, the Brymja falls off and grants the most beautiful view of the setting moon in all of Nightsdeep.

### 		**Dahab Al Mamlakah**

The Golden Kingdom was a major trade partner of Nightsdeep. Dahab Al Mamlakah’s burning sands and strange architecture called many an adventurer through the valley of bandits to its odd cities and customs. Pilgrims told of cities where worship of Saluwan was enforced by law. There were also tales of places where Saluwan was merely one god in an entire pantheon. Either way, the golden kingdom was a beautiful and vibrant place. It is a pity that no one knows what has become of Dahab Al Mamlakah. Those who survive the valley of bandits have never returned with news.

# Magic and Nightsdeep

Once, men were able to wield Great Magic. They were able to control the elements. They summoned mythical beasts of nightmares and fever dreams. They held in their palm the very powers of creation and destruction itself. They were like gods among mere mortals. With their power they amassed tremendous armies of dreadful warriors and used them to march across the blasted landscape in search of the next great conquest. Mad sorcerers erected strange towers in honor of their own bloated egos. Conflict was inevitable. The Great War brought death and destruction to every corner of creation. In its ashes, the Great Magic was sealed off, never to be used by mortals again. Now, all low magic is a mere shadow of what once was.

## 	**Miracles and the Old Gods**

Saluwan may listen to the prayers of the faithful but he doesn’t seem to act on their prayers. Largely, miracles from Saluwan just don’t seem to happen anymore. Most faithful would say that while Saluwan slumbers, he wants his people to stand on their own. Some would say that that is simply a cop out and that Saluwan has been dead for a long time. The biggest secret in Nightsdeep is that the Old gods however, aren’t silent. Whether peering out of the depths of the deepest oceans or waiting on an old dusty crossroad, the Old gods are still active. They hunger for the faithful to call upon them, to pray to them and to sacrifice to them. Because they hunger to be free.

These gods aren’t very picky about how they are called, although a great many particular rituals do exist. Following a ritual makes the invocation simpler in that it lends an air of legitimacy. The important thing is that the request must be done with complete faith. The Old gods demand absolute devotion. As such, to ask a request of Marka may mean cutting open your own belly or worse, cutting open the belly of someone else. Taking back a deal with the Old gods is like politely asking a wildfire to stop burning a forest. What is done now is done forever. That said, the Old gods are capable of nearly anything as long as their price is met. The price however is always steeper than the reward.

## 	**Blessings Of Saluwan**

The secret sect called the Blade of Saluwan is devoted to bringing the light to all people and driving out the darkness that enslaves humanity. To that end, they have several miracles that they can work that help fight against vampires. None of the blessings are always on. They take focus and a strong will to activate. This rule however doesn’t seem to hold the first time that the blessing manifests. The first time seems to be random and can cause the person a great deal of problems if they aren’t prepared. Not everyone within the bloodlines is granted the blessing and it seems that some are only granted one blessing and others are granted all of them.

### 		**See the Truth**

By focusing their mind, the people holding the blessings of Saluwan can see through illusions at the truth that lay within. This means that they essentially peer through any type of illusion. Unknowingly blessed people may find themselves particularly distraught when they look at what they believed was a normal person and see through a vampire’s facade at the rotting husk beneath.  
*“be not deceived by lies or blinded to the truth”*

### 		**Blessing of Blood**

In times of need or sometimes even in strange offensive ways, those with the blessing of blood seem to be able to cause their blood to have extremely adverse reactions to vampires. When this blessing is active, a simple touch will cause a vampire extreme discomfort and eventually burn them. The blood itself is even more potent and can cause a vampire to burst into flames when coming into contact with it.  
*“hold the flames within you and extend your palm to your brother”*

### 		**Saluwan's Wrath**

It is believed that those with the blessing of Saluwan’s wrath were meant to be leaders to others of the bloodline. Their words can pull at the emotions of those who hear them causing them to become braver and sometimes even ignore wounds that would give anyone else pause. This blessing is dangerous though as the voice can sometimes inspire a great, mindless rage within a vampire.  
*“I whisper and your walls crumble before me”*

### 		**Cleanse the Mind**

Some vampires and unholy magic can cause the mind to become influenced by others. Whether it’s the vampiric gift that drives one to do things against their will or other unholy means, those with the blessing called cleanse the mind are able to focus their spirit and purge that influence. It is written in the Havamael, that Saluwan came upon a woman suffering some sort of demonic possession. He put his hand upon the woman and tore the soul of a screaming beast from within her. At that point the woman was returned to her normal self. Though no mortal seems to be able to cleanse the mind of another, those with this blessing can free themselves.  
*“a clouded mind is poison for the soul”*

### 		**Walk the Flames**

Saluwan was said to be completely spared from the ravages of fire. Those with this blessing seem to have a shard of that. The belief is that Saluwan approves of your purity of spirit by granting some protection against fire. Though no man can simply ignore fire completely, those with this blessing seem to be able to ignore its effects for a time. Men have been able to leap into burning buildings to save children and emerge unscathed.  
*“Saluwan strode through the burning temple with rage in his heart”*

### 		**Mark the Path**

When the gifts were being granted, it is believed that among those who received the gifts were a mute boy. To this boy, Saluwan granted the ability to communicate and coordinate his brethren. No one is certain on why the runes are invisible to all but the chosen and no one knows why the runes are able to be understood by all. These mysteries seem to fade to the background when the blessed realizes that they can now communicate with total immunity from unworthy eyes. The runes are simple concepts like safe, vampire and meeting but they are enough.  
*“The path of righteousness is marked with the word of Saluwan”*

## 	**The Circle of Holun**

The gifts of magic come with secrets that eat away at your very soul. The circle has 5 points that correspond to the 5 types of magic. Each type has five levels that gradually increase in power. When learning a type of magic, the apprentice risks their very mind and each new revelation only makes the strain on the mage worse. The most powerful practitioners of magic are twisted men and women indeed. So while the rewards can be very great indeed, the risks are just as extreme. Below are not the only spells possible, there are many hidden tomes with all manner of twisted knowledge. These are just a sampling.

### 		**The Eye**

The eye of Holun revolves around information. Gathering secrets, speaking to the dead and learning things that man was not meant to know. To that end, The point of the eye is to make a connection. All of these spells require a vital link to the subject. Hair and preferred objects are powerful while a drop of blood or a heart is most powerful of all. The more powerful the result, the more gruesome the cost.

1. Whisper across the distance \- Send a message to the subject despite any distance.  
2. See through the veil \- See what the subject sees despite any distance.  
3. Words left unspoken \- Receive one answer truthfully, even from the dead.  
4. See the unspeakable \- Grant the subject visions of their own death.  
5. Holun sees all \- Peers into the very soul of the subject, learning their darkest desires.

### 		**The Claw**

The claw of Holun revolves around the wilds. Calling beasts, commanding them and even becoming one are all within the purview of this point on the circle. All of these spells require the animal in question and the most powerful spells require its sacrifice.

1. Calm the beast \- calm any beast into a more docile state.  
2. Call the wilds \- Sense and call the nearest beast to your aid.  
3. Command the beast \- Any beast that you can see will obey your commands for a time.  
4. Lead the pack \- Call upon a pack, swarm or flock of the beast of your choosing.  
5. Unleash the beast \- sacrifice an animal, wrap yourself in its still-warm skin and become it for a time.

### 		**The Fang**

It is said that the fangs of Holun are dripping with the venom of a thousand violent deaths. The point of the fang is rooted in the venom of Holun. These spells are all about weakening foes, poisoning them and bringing ruin upon their bodies. In order to affect a specific target, the mage must touch the victim unless otherwise noted.

1. Noxious air \- causes the subject to feel extreme nausea and discomfort.  
2. Blessing of Holun \- apply an incurable poison to an object or the mage’s own lips. The object or kiss must be received voluntarily.  
3. Crippling curse \- create an object that can cause terrible pain to a subject.  
4. Blight of flesh \- the subject begins to suffer from a debilitating disease that ends in the subject’s flesh falling off.  
5. Swarm of rats \- A swarm of plague ridden rats descends upon the subject area.

### 		**The Blood**

Blood is one half of life itself. The blood animates the body and gives the flesh presence. The point of blood is to manipulate this to the ends of the mage. These spells are about controlling the body itself. All of these spells require blood from the victim.

1. Peace of suffering \- The mage can anesthetize the subject and block out pain or they can cause the pain to feel more intense and acute.  
2. Bend flesh \- This allows the mage to mend grievous wounds or cause them.  
3. Crawling flesh \- The mage can adjust and repair or modify the internal organs of the subject.  
4. Weave bone \- The subject’s very body is malleable under the will of the mage.  
5. Servant of blood \- Create a living servant from the bodies of your subjects

### 		**The Breath**

The breath is the other half of life. It is the spark that ignites the body and empowers the soul. It is the very essence of the individual. This point is all about manipulating the individual and their very souls. In order to do these spells, the mage must give of themselves. It requires greater and greater sacrifice.

1. Hex \- The subject finds themselves more likely to drop things, forget, etc.  
2. Shattering whisper \- The subject must obey any simple command given by the mage.  
3. Bend Mind \- This allows the mage to make small changes to the subject’s memories.  
4. Enslave mind \- Slowly erode the will of the subject until they have no thought but to serve.  
5. Possession \- The mage must command the enslaved subject to plunge a special dagger into the subject’s heart. The mage will then transfer their consciousness into the subject.

## 	**Lost Arcane Secrets**

Though the power of the Great Magic is gone from the world, low magic still seeps in. Some sorcerers have learned to harness this low magic. Though the practice is almost dead, it is still possible to find hidden scraps of secret knowledge if you are willing to look in the forgotten places of the world. Low magic is a shadow of the power that Great magic was and as such its effects are simpler and often much more subtle.

In order to use low magic a sorcerer literally gives a bit themselves. The working of magic is in direct violation to the powerful bans that are in place and so even the slightest spell causes the sorcerer fatigue. It isn’t merely a matter of knowing the right words and drawing the correct symbols, a sorcerer must prepare themselves. This is done by drawing the correct runes upon the skin. When done correctly, the rune will attach itself like a kind of tattoo. This prepares the spell. Then, when the spell is to be used, the sorcerer says the right incantation and focuses herself. When the spell is used, the rune vanishes from their body.

| Rune | Meaning | Possibilities |
| ----- | ----- | ----- |
| ![1.gif][image2] | Renewal, Rejuvenation, Internal Powers | Healing minor wounds, repairing equipment, strengthening walls |
| ![3.gif][image3] | Protection, warding, defensive | Sense someone coming, Prevent evil influences, Ward away evil |
| ![6.gif][image4] | Knowledge, understanding, learning |  |
| ![10.gif][image5] | Restriction, Needs, Air | Breathe underwater, restrict movement, inspire hunger |
| ![11.gif][image6] | Ice, stasis, difficulty | Cause someone to shake from cold, make someone very tired, calm someone |
| ![14.gif][image7] | Memory, Chance, Problem solving | Share a memory, increase the chances of something happening, Open a lock |

# Science of Nightsdeep

The scientific method is new to Nightsdeep. Those who try to practice it are often referred to as Rationalists. A rationalist believes that all things can be explained through natural processes that could be understood if one simply studied the phenomena well enough. This belief colors their view of everything from the vampire true lords to the hollow themselves. Scientific rigor however is less strictly adhered to, however. This means that repeatability isn't as important as results.

## **Medicine and taboos**

A rationalist that specializes in attempting to heal the sick and injured is often called a Stitch. Stitches live in a strange space socially. On the one hand, they have seen some measure of success and when a person is in dire need, they will turn to anyone who may help. That gives the Stitch access to people from across the socioeconomic strata. On the other hand, Stitches cut open people and deal with blood. This pushes known stitches to the edges of social groups because most people don't want to openly associate with a stitch.

## **Rationalism unleashed**

Some Rationalists are beyond the cutting edge of technology and science. These Rationalists push the bounds of morality and even sanity. Mad Rationalists are one of the reasons that Rationalism isn't embraced by most people (aside from the natural inclination to doubt that “all things could have answers”). These Rationalists push their specialization to new heights or lows. For some, kidnapping and experimenting on innocent victims is just a price of progress.

# Creatures of Nightsdeep

Nightsdeep is the kind of place where a howl at night is likely a werewolf at your door. A place where inviting a stranger to shelter them from the rain can mean having your life drained completely by a vampire. There are all manner of strange creatures and fantastic monsters that plague the land.

## 	**The Hollow Ones**

The hollow ones are a strange alien hive-mind of green flame that possesses the living body of a person, animal and sometimes even plant. It fills it with it’s green flame and grants it entirely new properties. All hollows are one and don’t seem to be limited by distance. This means that there is no communication to intercept, nothing to negotiate with and what one knows or sees, all know. An individual hollow one doesn’t exhibit much intelligence though the more hollow in one area, the more cunning the hollow ones become as a whole. The hollow ones don’t even know that humanity really exists. They are a force of nature hell bent on making all living things become part of it.

### 		**Traits of the Hollow Ones**

The hollow ones are no more strong or fast than they were before. In fact individual hollows are rather weak in that they do not possess any abilities or skills that they had in the past. A once competent hunter and tracker will now bumble aimlessly, a shadow of what they were. They do however possess such incredible regenerative abilities that killing one is a matter of completely destroying the body. Even decapitation may only slow it for a moment as it comes back together in a disgusting sort of way. It is known that the hollow eats the flesh of the living, what is unknown by the common people is why some are not eaten at all but instead dragged away.

### 		**How are more hollow made**

Those who are dragged off by the hollow are taken back to the deep where they undergo a terrible ordeal as their mind is torn asunder and all their knowledge, skills and personality are assimilated into the thing below. The tiny sliver of self that remains is snuffed out under the sheer size and power of the combined minds already consumed. Once a person becomes hollow, they are forever changed and cannot be saved. Only destruction can bring peace to their poor souls. Vampires, being dead, are unable to become hollow. In fact, though the hollow may physically see a vampire, it doesn’t perceive the vampire at all. It’s as if the vampire is seen on the same level as a stone.

### 		**What is in the Deep?**

Within the deep is the great, enormous body of a sleeping alien being of unimaginable destructive power. This being knows only to consume souls and make them its own. Its enormous body is contorted into unknowable shapes with appendages that defy description. Simply gazing upon the body of the being has driven men mad even before the assault on their minds begins. Physically the being within the deep is truly massive but, it is in fact merely a child compared to the growth that it will eventually undergo. With each mind fed to it, it grows ever so slightly. If it were to awaken and rise it would already tower over mountains. The thing within the deep doesn’t destroy out of malice, it destroys because that is its very nature.

## 	**The Risen**

The risen is a name given to a class of creature composed of dead flesh given life by infernal science. They may be incredibly beautiful or they may be patchwork beings made of the flesh of multiple cadavers. Some roses are even made of animal body parts or machine parts integrated into their grotesque forms. Anyone who comes across a risen creature is almost universally put off as simply being around one will make a person feel like their skin is crawling. Each rose is unique. Some may be as intelligent as a cunning animal, others may be fully cognizant and aware of their disgusting situation. They are a parody of life missing a soul. Inevitably driven mad by their unfinished nature.

### 		**Infernal Science**

Risen are given life by infernal science. A strange type of magic consisting of using vile liquids and terrible machines. The infernal science seems like a twisted and corrupted form of alchemy. Where alchemy seeks to unlock the secrets of the physical world, infernal science wants to unlock the secrets of life and death. Practitioners of infernal science, called scientists, believe that the world and everything in it is able to be controlled and understood. They want to wield powers held only by gods and will stop at nothing to have them. Almost all infernal scientists are insane and out of touch with the world, concerned only about their experiments. Though no official cabal exists, it is common for a scientist to take on an apprentice or two at most in order to carry on the great work.

### 		**Why Create a Risen?**

Ultimately, the goal of creating a rose is to create the perfect life form. A pure and perfect simulacrum of ordinary human life in an immortal shell. Though every scientist has different reasons for wanting to do so, many scientists currently believe that an army of risen is the only way to defeat the hollow ones. The worst part is that given the fact that the hollow ones completely ignore the dead; the scientists may actually be right.

# Places in Nightsdeep

## 	**Skaldfel**

### 		**The Lovers (political and commercial)**

#### 			Plaza of the Lovers

The Plaza of the Lovers occupies the heart of Old Nightsdeep, a circular space paved with worn cobblestones that gleam faintly under the perpetual twilight filtering through the city’s towering structures. Once a vibrant marketplace and gathering place for all walks of life, it now bears an air of melancholy beauty, steeped in whispered histories and lingering shadows.

A central fountain, carved from dark grey basalt depicting entwined lovers eternally embracing, stands dry and silent, its water diverted decades ago during a particularly harsh winter that never truly ended. Around the fountain’s perimeter, crumbling stone benches offer fleeting respite, often occupied by solitary figures lost in thought or pairs sharing hushed conversations.

The plaza is framed by buildings of varying heights and architectural styles, remnants of Nightsdeep’s tumultuous past: grand merchant houses with faded frescoes, decaying temples dedicated to forgotten gods, and the stark grey walls of a former military barracks now repurposed into apartments. Ivy climbs many facades, softening the harshness but also hinting at neglect.

Small stalls occasionally appear, peddling trinkets or offering simple refreshments, though their presence is fleeting and often tied to seasonal festivals or rumored good fortune. The air itself feels heavy with unspoken promises and bittersweet memories \- a place where love was declared, lost, and mourned under the watchful gaze of Nightsdeep’s eternal gloom. Locals say if you listen closely on a still night, you can hear echoes of laughter and music from a time when the Plaza truly lived up to its name.

#### 			The Glass House

The Glass House is an anomaly in Nightsdeep \- a shimmering beacon of unnatural light and impossible architecture that seems to defy the city’s pervasive gloom. Rising five stories high, it’s constructed entirely of panes of intricately crafted glass, fused together with a silvery metal that hums faintly with arcane energy. The glass isn’t clear; instead, it filters the dim light into shifting patterns of emerald, sapphire, and amethyst hues that dance across its surface, making it appear to breathe.

Unlike the crumbling stone and soot-stained buildings surrounding it, The Glass House is pristine and flawless, reflecting a warped image of Nightsdeep’s own decay. Its interior remains largely obscured from view, though glimpses through the glass reveal impossible geometries:  floating staircases, rooms that seem to bend at unnatural angles, and swirling patterns of light that hint at something extraordinary within.

A small, wrought-iron gate guards its entrance, always locked and patrolled by silent, impeccably dressed individuals who offer no explanation for its existence. Locals whisper that The Glass House is a prison, a laboratory, or perhaps even a gateway to another realm entirely. No one knows who built it, what purpose it serves, or if anyone truly lives within its shimmering walls; only that its unsettling beauty and impenetrable mystery cast a long shadow over Nightsdeep’s already enigmatic landscape. It radiates an aura of both captivating wonder and profound unease, a constant reminder that some secrets are best left undisturbed.

#### 			Tower of Art

The Tower of Art juts skyward from the highest point in Nightsdeep’s Scholar’s Quarter, a slender spire of mismatched stone and shimmering obsidian that seems to twist slightly as you gaze upon it. It is not built in any conventional architectural style; instead, it appears to have grown organically over centuries, with additions haphazardly layered onto earlier structures; a testament to the eccentric visionaries who have called it home.

Its exterior is covered in a chaotic tapestry of carvings: grotesque gargoyles leering from shadowed corners, intricate floral patterns interwoven with cryptic runes, and fragmented depictions of scenes both beautiful and disturbing. Windows of every conceivable shape and size punctuate the tower’s surface \- some stained glass depicting mythical creatures, others simple apertures offering glimpses into cluttered workshops filled with strange apparatuses.

A constant stream of vibrant light spills from these windows, accompanied by a cacophony of sounds: the rhythmic clang of hammers against metal, the frantic scribbling of quills on parchment, the mournful strains of unfamiliar instruments, and bursts of excited laughter mixed with frustrated sighs. The air around the tower hums with creative energy, thick enough to taste.

A narrow, winding staircase carved directly into the rock face is the only apparent entrance, guarded by a rotating roster of students and eccentric professors who seem more interested in their own pursuits than in deterring visitors. Rumor has it that within its walls lie workshops dedicated to every conceivable art form \- from enchanting pigments and animating clay to sculpting illusions and composing melodies that can manipulate emotions. The Tower of Art is not merely a place of learning; it’s a crucible where imagination is forged, dreams are realized (and often shattered), and the very fabric of reality is subtly altered.

### 		**The Bear (residential and middle class)**

#### 			The Red Room

The Red Room isn't so much \*in\* Nightsdeep as it \*is\* Nightsdeep distilled—a concentrated essence of decadence, intrigue, and hushed power. Tucked away within a labyrinthine network of tunnels beneath the Merchant’s Guild, its entrance is unmarked, known only to those who receive an invitation; or possess the cunning to find it.

The club itself occupies a cavernous chamber bathed in the warm glow of crimson-shaded lanterns, casting elongated shadows that dance across walls draped with heavy velvet tapestries depicting scenes of lavish revelry and veiled secrets. The air is thick with the scent of expensive perfumes, exotic spices from distant lands, and the faintest hint of something illicit—perhaps a rare alchemical blend or a forbidden pleasure.

Tables crafted from polished obsidian are scattered throughout the room, each surrounded by plush velvet armchairs and attended to by silent, impeccably dressed servers who seem to anticipate every need before it’s even voiced. The clientele is an exclusive mix of Nightsdeep's elite: wealthy merchants, influential nobles, shadowy figures from the criminal underworld, and artists pushing the boundaries of accepted taste. Conversation flows in hushed tones, punctuated by the clinking of crystal glasses filled with potent elixirs and the occasional burst of laughter that quickly dies down as if swallowed by the room’s oppressive atmosphere.

A raised stage at one end hosts performances ranging from mesmerizing dancers to unsettling illusionists, all designed to titillate and bewilder. Above it hangs a single, massive chandelier crafted from ruby glass, its light reflecting in the eyes of those who linger within: eyes that hold secrets best left buried. The Red Room is not merely a place for socializing; it's a stage where fortunes are made and lost, alliances forged and broken, and reputations carefully cultivated or irrevocably destroyed.

#### 			Eklund Theatre

The Eklund Theatre isn't merely a building; it’s an experience: a glittering monument to House Eklund’s dedication to spectacle and extravagance. Situated in the heart of Nightsdeep’s entertainment district, its façade is a riot of sculpted obsidian and polished brass, constantly shifting with intricate clockwork mechanisms that display scenes from current performances or simply shimmer with dazzling light patterns.

The main entrance is flanked by two colossal statues of mythical creatures crafted from shimmering moonstone, their eyes appearing to follow passersby. Inside, the grand foyer boasts a vaulted ceiling painted with constellations that actually \*move\*, mimicking the night sky above Nightsdeep. Chandeliers fashioned from countless crystals cast a kaleidoscopic glow upon plush velvet seating and ornate marble floors.

The auditorium itself is circular, designed to ensure every seat offers an unobstructed view of the stage which often incorporates elaborate moving sets, holographic projections, and even controlled bursts of theatrical fog and simulated weather effects. Luxurious private boxes line the walls, each equipped with its own miniature bar and a dedicated attendant eager to cater to the whims of Nightsdeep’s elite.

Whispers say that hidden passages and secret chambers weave throughout the Theatre's foundations, used for quick costume changes, surprise entrances, and clandestine meetings; all part of the Eklunds' commitment to an unforgettable night out.

#### 			The Row of Roses

The Row of Roses isn't simply a street; it’s Nightsdeep's most renowned and romantic thoroughfare. Lined on both sides by towering buildings crafted from pale sandstone, the street derives its name from the meticulously cultivated rose bushes that climb trellises along every facade. These aren't ordinary roses either, but genetically engineered blooms exhibiting an astonishing array of colors, from deep indigo, shimmering gold, vibrant crimson, and even a rare, luminous silver.

The scent is intoxicating, a constant blend of floral sweetness and subtle spice that hangs heavy in the air. Gas lamps cast a warm, flickering glow upon the cobblestone pavement at night, enhancing the already magical atmosphere. Small boutiques selling perfumes, handcrafted jewelry, and unique artistic creations nestle between elegant tea rooms and exclusive restaurants.

Carriages are the preferred mode of transport here; the gentle clip-clop of hooves against stone is a familiar sound, mingling with the soft strains of music drifting from open windows. The Row of Roses is considered a place for courtship, quiet reflection, or simply enjoying a moment of beauty in the bustling heart of Nightsdeep; a sanctuary dedicated to elegance and charm.

#### 			Plaza of the Saints

The Plaza of the Saints isn't grand or ornate; it’s a place worn smooth by time and countless footsteps. Located in the heart of Skaldfel, it’s less a formal square and more a natural gathering space carved out amongst the tightly packed homes and workshops that cling to the hillside.

The ground is uneven, a patchwork of grey flagstones interspersed with patches of hardy moss and wildflowers that stubbornly push through the cracks. A central stone basin, often dry but occasionally filled with rainwater after a storm, acts as an impromptu fountain. Around its perimeter are several weathered benches made from roughly hewn logs and carved stones, offering places to rest for weary miners or chatty families.

Dominating one side of the plaza is a simple, unadorned shrine built into the rock face. The namesake "Saints" being local heroes revered for their resilience during Skaldfel's early struggles. Offerings of carved stones and dried herbs are often left at its base. The air here smells faintly of stone dust, woodsmoke from nearby hearths, and occasionally, the sweet scent of baking bread. It’s a place of quiet industry, simple connection, and the enduring spirit of Skaldfel.

### 		**The Loom (artisans and craftsmen)**

#### 			The Artificer’s Guild

The Artificer's Guild isn't a grand palace or imposing structure; it's more akin to a sprawling workshop complex that has organically grown over decades, clinging to the side of a rocky outcrop overlooking the lower city. It’s a place where practicality and ingenuity reign supreme, and aesthetics take a backseat to function.

The building itself is a chaotic jumble of interconnected stone buildings, timber frames, and haphazardly added extensions. Pipes, gears, and strange contraptions jut out from walls at odd angles, connected by a network of walkways and scaffolding that crisscross the area. Smoke billows constantly from several chimneys, carrying the scent of metalworking, alchemical concoctions, and occasionally, something vaguely explosive. Patches of moss and climbing vines soften the rough stone exterior, hinting at the wild nature of the surrounding landscape.

Inside is even more chaotic than outside. The main hall is a vast, echoing space filled with workbenches piled high with tools, components, and half-finished projects. Sparks fly from forges, gears whir incessantly, and the air hums with the energy of creation. Smaller workshops branch off from the main hall, each dedicated to a specific craft: clockwork mechanisms, enchanted weaponry, alchemical potions, and more. The walls are plastered with diagrams, schematics, and hastily scribbled notes. Dust motes dance in shafts of light filtering through grimy windows, illuminating the faces of Artificers hunched over their work, lost in their own worlds of innovation.

The Artificer’s Guild is a hive of activity: a place where dreams are forged into reality, and where the line between science, magic, and sheer invention blurs completely. It's loud, messy, and utterly captivating to anyone with an interest in creating something new.

#### 			Oleifr’s Master Forge

Oleifr Sorensen is a craftsman of unparalleled skill but also a man of an unparalleled temper. His angry exploits are quite legendary among the people of the looms district. If not for his amazing skill with his forge, no one would accept his abrasive manner. As it is, he is barely tolerated by the nobility. He is a large older man with a stooped posture from so many years at the anvil. His large hands are harsh and calloused and he treats any handshake as a contest. The only person able to get through to him when he’s in a rage is his wife. A small old woman with a strange, almost regal bearing. Her voice never rises above almost a whisper but she can silence Oleifr with a simple word.

The shop itself is a jumble of sheets of metal, completed pieces of armor and weapons stacked in what looks like careless piles. Oleifr however has a system that only he understands. He is able to say without looking, how many sheets of metal he has or where a particular item is. His shop is a squat, stone building with most of it given over to the forge. A couple boys run back and forth outside between huge piles of wooden logs and a square hole that feeds into the furnace.

#### 			The Loyal Gallows

The Loyal Gallows isn’t inviting; it’s enduring. Hewn directly into the base of a crumbling cliff face on the edge of the Docklands, its existence feels less like construction and more like stubborn defiance against Nightsdeep's decay.

The tavern’s facade is rough-hewn stone, perpetually damp with sea spray and shadowed by the overhanging cliffs. A single, flickering lantern hangs above a heavy wooden door reinforced with iron bands, a clear message about who's welcome and what kind of clientele it caters to. Above the door, crudely carved into the stone, is the tavern’s namesake: a gallows framed by two crossed cutlasses. It’s not subtle.

The air inside is thick with the smells of stale ale, brine, cheap tobacco, and something vaguely unpleasant that lingers near the hearth. The main room is dimly lit by oil lamps casting long, dancing shadows on the low ceiling. Tables are scarred and sticky, bolted to the stone floor for stability (and to discourage moving them during brawls). A raised platform serves as a makeshift stage, often occupied by struggling musicians or weary storytellers. The fireplace dominates one wall, radiating a meager warmth that barely combats the damp chill seeping in from the sea. Behind the bar, a gruff-looking proprietor polishes tankards with a practiced indifference to his patrons.

The Loyal Gallows is a haven for those who dwell in the shadows: sailors looking for oblivion, mercenaries seeking contracts, and anyone wanting to disappear for a while. It's rough, rowdy, and utterly unapologetic about its reputation as Nightsdeep’s most dangerous and reliable watering hole. You come here for drink, company of questionable character, and maybe a fight; you don't come for pleasantries.

### 		**The Sword (docks and warehouses)**

#### 			The Gentleman’s Bet

The Gentleman’s Bet is an anomaly in Nightsdeep, a place striving for elegance amidst the pervasive gloom. It stands on a slightly elevated corner in the Sword, attempting to project an air of refined respectability that struggles against the city’s inherent grit.

The building itself is constructed from dark grey stone, meticulously cleaned and maintained, with ornate wrought-iron balconies overlooking the street. A sign depicting two stylized figures shaking hands hangs above the entrance, subtly hinting at the tavern's name and theme. Soft light spills from the windows, a stark contrast to the flickering lanterns of surrounding establishments.

Stepping inside is like entering another world. The air is noticeably cleaner, scented with beeswax polish and subtle spices rather than ale and sweat. Richly colored tapestries depicting scenes of noble hunts and lavish feasts adorn the walls. Tables are covered in crisp linen cloths, and polished silverware gleams under the soft glow of crystal chandeliers. A grand piano sits in a corner, occasionally played by a resident musician. While not opulent, it aims for understated luxury.

The inn rooms follow suit: comfortably furnished with plush carpets, comfortable beds draped with fine fabrics, and private bathing facilities (a rarity in Nightsdeep). Each room is named after a famous gambler from Nightsdeep’s history.

The Gentleman's Bet caters to merchants, visiting dignitaries, and those who prefer their entertainment accompanied by a measure of decorum, though the occasional shady deal or high-stakes game can still be found within its walls. It’s an oasis of relative civility in Nightsdeep, but one that always carries the unspoken awareness that appearances can be deceiving.

#### 			Vinter Shipwrights

Vinter Shipwrights is more than just a shipyard; it's a sprawling complex that dominates the eastern docks of Darkholm. The air hangs thick with the smell of salt, tar and freshly cut timber. Massive cranes groan as they lift enormous timbers into place on half-finished hulls. A constant hammering rhythm echoes across the yard mingling with the shouts of foremen and the rasping of saws.

The main workshop is a cavernous space lit by oil lamps casting long shadows across the bustling activity within. Skilled shipwrights meticulously shape planks, fit masts and carve intricate details into figureheads. Smaller workshops branch off from the central area housing carpenters, sailmakers and riggers each specializing in their craft.

A network of canals crisscrosses the yard allowing for easy transport of materials and completed vessels to the open sea. Several smaller docks are reserved for repairs and smaller commissions while larger slips accommodate the construction of grand merchant ships and formidable warships for House Vinter’s ever-expanding fleet. The entire operation is overseen by Master Eldrin, a stern but fair man known for his uncompromising standards and deep knowledge of shipbuilding. Vinter Shipwrights represents not only House Vinter's wealth and power but also their commitment to maritime dominance.

#### 			The Preacher’s Rock

The Preacher's Rock isn't so much a building as it is a designated space; a large, flat outcropping of granite worn smooth by countless feet and weather. It sits at the intersection of several busy streets in the Sword, a natural amphitheater carved into the city’s uneven terrain.

The rock itself is roughly twenty feet across, stained with years of rain, chalk dust from hastily drawn signs, and the occasional splatter of something unidentifiable. A haphazard collection of crates, upturned barrels, and rickety wooden platforms surrounds it, providing makeshift stages for the various orators. A perpetually dusty sign hammered into the rock simply reads: "Speak Freely," marking this space as one of the few where people are allowed to speak somewhat openly.

The air around The Preacher’s Rock is a chaotic mix of fervent pronouncements, heckling shouts, philosophical debates, and general street noise. You'll hear everything from fire-and-brimstone sermons to political rants to rambling poetry; often all at the same time. The crowd that gathers fluctuates wildly; sometimes it's a small cluster of devout listeners, other times a boisterous throng eager for entertainment or confrontation.

A chipped stone basin near the rock provides water for those who wish to cleanse themselves before speaking (or argue with those who have). Scrawled on the rock’s surface are countless names, symbols, and slogans, a testament to the diverse voices that have used it over the years. The city guard generally tolerates the activity, but strict rules against inciting violence or public disorder are occasionally enforced, usually by a weary-looking officer attempting to maintain order amidst the din.

It’s a raw, unfiltered slice of Nightsdeep life, a place where anyone with something to say can have their moment, regardless of how unpopular or outlandish their message may be.

### 		**The Wheel (Slums)**

#### 			Carnival of the Grotesque

The Carnival of the Grotesque squats like a festering wound in the heart of the Wheel slums. It’s less a celebration and more a spectacle of desperation, a place where misery is packaged and sold for a few copper coins. The air vibrates with discordant music, a wheezing calliope battling against the cries of hawkers and the nervous laughter of onlookers.

Tents of faded crimson and sickly yellow sprawl haphazardly across the muddy ground, their edges patched with scraps of canvas and desperation. Garish banners depicting distorted figures promise wonders and horrors within, often exceeding what's actually on display. The smell is a potent mix of sawdust, stale beer, cheap perfume attempting to mask something far less pleasant, and a pervasive undercurrent of despair.

Inside the tents, "exhibits" are presented with blatant disregard for their dignity. A “Bearded Lady” hides her face in shame, while a man with mismatched limbs is forced to perform clumsy tricks for amusement. Stories, often fabricated or embellished, accompany each display designed to evoke pity or disgust depending on the audience's preference.

A ringmaster, a greasy character named Silas with eyes that seem to absorb all light, orchestrates the proceedings with a practiced cruelty. He thrives on the discomfort and fascination of the crowd, his voice booming over the din as he introduces each “marvel.” The Carnival of the Grotesque is not entertainment, it's an exploitation, a grim reflection of Nightsdeep’s underbelly where even suffering has a price.
